text:
anya: FYI @samir @marco we're onboarding tenant 'tidal' into ap-southeast-9 (new region). Need accelerator + network ceilings pre-provisioned. Target go-live 2026-04-01. Ask: p5 instances x8 (inference runtime), g5 instances x40 (burst), ENI limit bumped to 500, and IPv4 pool for NAT (we currently rely on NAT gw). Any objections or additional requirements?

samir: pls paste account/org id and current quota snapshot. Do we need reserved capacity or just on-demand for now? Also need expected concurrent jobs / peak vCPU footprint.

anya: Account: 987654321098, Org: tidal-prod. For now on-demand is fine, but we'll convert some to reserved/dedicated if performance needs it. Peak concurrency: ~200 inference workers, avg seq len 512. Expected sustained token throughput ~6M tokens/day. Current service-quotas output: 
```
Service Quotas - ap-southeast-9
EC2 G5 instances: 0
EC2 P5 instances: 0
ENI limit (regional): 50
Elastic IPs: 5

Note: VPC subnets present but only 3 private IPs available per subnet currently.
```

eng-infra-bot: automated scan: detected missing accelerator entitlements for this account in ap-southeast-9. Recommended next step: open AWS Support case with service-quotas accelerate request AND attach workload runbook.

marco: subnet/NAT questions: are we going to put inference nodes in private subnets behind NAT? If so we need NAT GW elastic IPs and a NAT throughput plan — p5s have high egress. Also confirm if we need 25Gbps ENIs (some g5 variants use 25/50Gbps). If using ENI scaling, bump secondary private IPs per instance.

anya: yes private subnets behind NAT. We'll likely use 25Gbps ENIs for g5.xlarge-ish nodes. I'll adjust subnet IP plan to add /22. NAT EIP needs to be ~10 now, maybe more later.

samir: here's a support template I usually use — paste into AWS Support case (Service Quotas -> Request): 
```
We are requesting increases for the following resources in region ap-southeast-9 for account 987654321098 (tidal-prod):
- EC2 p5 instances: Limit -> 8 (current 0)
- EC2 g5 instances: Limit -> 40 (current 0)
- Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI) regional limit: Limit -> 500 (current 50)
- Elastic IP addresses: Limit -> 50 (current 5)
Reason: We are onboarding a production inference workload (Redwood tenant 'tidal') with expected 200 concurrent workers, average seq length 512, and sustained token throughput ~6M/day. Instances will be in private subnets behind NAT GW; please include any recommended adjustments for ENI per-instance secondary IPs.
Please expedite this request; target go-live 2026-04-01. Contact: anya@redwood.ai, infra slack: #eng-infra.
```

katie: cost heads-up: if they keep 40 g5s on-demand that's a big monthly run rate. Suggest we propose a staged increase: 10 g5s initially, scale to 40 with canary and auto-burst. Also discuss Dedicated pools / Reserved if they'd commit. I can run a quick cost projection if you want. :money_with_wings:

anya: good point. For now request the full ceilings so we can scale when needed, but start with 10 g5 + 4 p5 in prod. I'll note staged usage in the support case.

samir: also open an internal infra ticket to prepare subnet expansion and NAT EIP procurement. I'll run a quick ENI vs IP-per-instance calc.

eng-infra-bot: created internal ticket INFRA-4592: subnet expansion / NAT EIP prep for tidal-prod (assigned: marco).

marco: acknowledged INFRA-4592. I'll provision new /22 subnets across 3 AZs and request +10 EIPs. Any preference on AZ balancing?

anya: balance across AZs please, aim to avoid single AZ concentration.

anya: opened AWS support case: case id 12345678901. Copied the template. Will paste updates here.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support case 12345678901 created. Initial response ETA: 48 hours.

(36 hours later)

aws-support-bot: AWS response: We can approve ENI increase to 500 and g5 instances to 20 immediately. P5 quota requests need entitlement review and will take up to 7 business days. Please provide architecture diagram and workload perf summary to speed p5 review.

anya: thanks — approved partial. I'll attach the architecture + perf report for p5 review. We've got enough g5 to start scale tests.

samir: thanks for the update. Once g5 are live we'll run gradual traffic and watch for ENI exhaustion. Marco coordinate with networking on NAT EIPs.

anya: will do. Closing here for now; will follow up when p5 entitlements come through. :white_check_mark:
